centralClaim: An aircraft equipped with Joby Aviation's autonomy technology flew across the United States with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot.
sendTest: Un avion a traversé les États-Unis sans que personne touche les commandes. 3 199 miles, décollages et atterrissages compris.

corroboration.quote: The aircraft flew 3,199 miles with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot, concluding the eastbound leg of its month-long tour in North Carolina's Outer Banks, near the site of the Wright brothers' first powered flight.
An aircraft equipped with Joby Aviation's autonomy technology flew more than 3,100 miles across the United States without a human pilot taking control at any point, the company said Friday.

caption:
Un avion a traversé les États-Unis sans que personne à bord ne touche les commandes.

Joby Aviation annonce que son appareil a volé 3 199 miles avec zéro intervention du pilote de sécurité assis à bord. Roulage, décollages, navigation et atterrissages : tout a été fait par la machine, sous supervision à distance depuis la Californie et une base aérienne de Caroline du Sud, jusqu'à 2 323 miles de là.

L'appareil. Un Cessna 208B Caravan modifié, équipé de la technologie de vol autonome de Joby.

Le détail qui n'est pas dans la vidéo. Le pilote à distance, lui, était vraiment le commandant de bord : c'est lui qui gérait les changements de plan de vol et qui parlait aux contrôleurs aériens par la radio de l'avion. Celui assis dans le cockpit pouvait reprendre la main et ne l'a pas fait.

Ce qui coince. C'est l'entreprise qui rapporte le résultat, et un pilote était bien à bord pour la conformité. Avant ce vol, le système comptait plus de 400 vols et 800 heures de vol automatisé.

Et ce n'est pas pour tes vacances : Joby cite le fret commercial, le transport médical, les secours en cas de catastrophe et la logistique de défense.

Et ce n'est pas fini. L'appareil repart maintenant vers l'ouest, avec des escales à Louisville, Salt Lake City et Portland.

Un avion de ligne sans pilote, tu monterais dedans, oui ou non ?

captionEvidence.quote: The aircraft flew 3,199 miles with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot, concluding the eastbound leg of its month-long tour in North Carolina's Outer Banks, near the site of the Wright brothers' first powered flight.

The aircraft, a converted Cessna Caravan, performed autonomous taxiing, takeoffs, route navigation, and landings under remote supervision from Joby's Autonomy Headquarters in California and Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, up to 2,323 miles away.

The journey demonstrated the operational capabilities of Joby's autonomy technology across a range of environments, supporting applications in commercial freight, medical transport, disaster response, and defense logistics.

Joby's autonomous technology is grounded in more than 400 flights and 800 automated flight hours in controlled and uncontrolled airspace, building on the mature autonomy stack acquired from Xwing in 2024.

The aircraft flew autonomously under the supervision of a remote pilot, who served as pilot in command, managed flight-plan updates and handled air traffic control communications through the aircraft's radios.
An onboard safety pilot remained available to take control but made no control inputs during the journey, according to Joby.
Known as the J208, the aircraft is a Cessna 208B Caravan fitted with Joby's autonomous flight technology.
A pilot was on board for compliance, but Joby said the aircraft performed the entire operation autonomously.

The aircraft will now begin its return westbound journey, including stops in Raleigh (KRDU), Fredericksburg/Washington, D.C. (KRMN), Louisville (KSDF), Wichita (KICT), Oklahoma City (KOKC), Salt Lake City (KSLC), and Portland (KPDX).

Following its transcontinental arrival, the J208 flew a historic low pass near the First Flight Monument at Kitty Hawk, honoring the site where Orville and Wilbur Wright ushered in the age of powered flight in 1903.
